items.summary: Paramount Skydance is selling about $52 billion of debt to finance its $81 billion cash purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery.

items.title: How Big Could Fair Isaac Stock's Next Fall Be?
items.summary: Fair Isaac (FICO) stock fell 27% in the past month with no company news to explain it. Equifax and TransUnion fell more than 20% too. If you hold the shares, you may wonder what a full market shock would do to them. Fair Isaac's record in past shocks can size the next fall, but only if the company that fell then is yours. So is today's Fair Isaac the same company that fell in past shocks.

items.title: Is Fair Isaac Stock Worth More Than Its Competitors?
items.summary: Fair Isaac (FICO), the maker of the FICO Score, beats Equifax, TransUnion and three other peers on revenue growth and operating margin. Yet its stock lost 59.3% over the past twelve months, the worst return in the group. So after that fall, is Fair Isaac stock worth more than its competitors.

items.title: Moody’s affirms Kazakhstan at Baa1 with stable outlook citing fiscal strength
items.summary: Investing.com -- Moody’s Ratings affirmed Kazakhstan’s long-term issuer ratings at Baa1 with a stable outlook, citing the sovereign’s robust balance sheet and low national debt burden as key buffers against external volatility.

items.title: Moody’s cuts Dave & Buster’s outlook to negative on sales slump
items.summary: Investing.com -- Moody’s Ratings has revised its credit outlook for Dave & Buster’s Entertainment (NASDAQ:PLAY) to negative from stable while affirming the company’s B3 corporate family rating. The revision signals growing credit risks tied to persistent operational weakness and execution hurdles surrounding the restaurant-entertainment chain's ongoing turnaround strategy.

items.title: S&P Global and Moody's Have Rated Debt for More Than 100 Years. Here's Why That Moat Still Holds.
items.summary: The two credit-rating giants remain resilient, evergreen investments.

items.title: These 4 Dividend Stocks Turn Customer Loyalty Into Growing Income
items.summary: Some businesses are so deeply embedded in daily operations that customers rarely bother to leave, and four companies have quietly built their dividends on exactly that kind of inertia. The question is whether sticky revenue alone is enough to keep payouts growing when the economy turns.
